body:
# the contributor audit: capacity means and a fixed density sandwich

This audit covers `candidate a26d4b26fb2a803f`
and `candidate 891aaf58ec0549c1`. Both pass. Neither is
a proof of OC, and neither supplies a universal all-direction center.

## 1. Endpoint capacity and its mean

For positive-dimensional endpoint bodies and a nonzero continuous
functional, every cap function is continuous and globally Lipschitz.
The section bound used for the latter is finite on a compact body,
including dimension one. The common Lipschitz constant survives the
infimum over tilts. The optimized endpoint tail is therefore the tail
of an atomless compactly supported measure of total mass the smaller
endpoint volume. The two support bounds in the source note include
their endpoints because supporting hyperplanes have zero body volume.

The pointwise midpoint indicator inequality has the correct direction:
a midpoint in a closed cap forces at least one source into its respective
closed cap, for EVERY tilt. Taking the infimum after this inequality is
legitimate. Stochastic domination compares measures with the SAME mass;
integrating over a common bounded support interval then compares their
first moments. No interchange of an infimum and an integral is made.

The derived law has total mass b+a, whereas the original mixed measure
has total a+b+c. These remain distinct in the transfer argument. Its
candidate y is an actual convex combination in the middle fiber. If an
ambient cap through or beyond y fails a target, monotonicity and the
one-sided mean comparison prove that the derived directional mean also
fails that target. This is an implication from an already failed point;
it does not construct a successful point.

For the five-dimensional example I separately checked the saved original
construction and cap inequality. In its relative volume units,
g_D,1=5r/6 and 1/6-g_D,1=103/3600<2/25. Thus the particular midpoint
mixture lies in the fixed first bad cap. Both endpoints are excluded by
that cap's actual integer tilt, and its middle cap mass is strictly less
than gamma_5(2+a)/2. The stochastic mean transfer proves exactly the
same absolute failure for the directional capacity mean. No approximate
value for the mean or the algebraic endpoint volume is used.

## 2. Sharp fixed-mass density characterization

Normalize the body volume to one. The cap-volume root is concave on
the scalar projection interval, and its expectation under uniform body
volume is d/(d+1). The extra submeasure pushes forward under the uniform
tail-rank map to a density between zero and one. Its masses on the cap
and its complement are respectively r and alpha-r. The two leftmost
quantile intervals in the source note give the exact increasing-function
bathtub minimum separately on these two regions. All Jensen factors
and the normalization 1+2 alpha are correct.

The feasible scalar domain is compact and nonempty. Its points have
s>0. At a purported minimizer with strict final inequality, decreasing
both s and r preserves the constraints when r>0; decreasing s alone
does so when r=0. These perturbations strictly lower the objective.
Thus the final inequality is an equality at every minimizer. The only
feasible point with s=1 has r=alpha and strict inequality, so minimizers
also have s<1. This includes alpha=0 and alpha=1: at alpha=1 the
domination constraints force r=s and the common decrement remains
feasible.

On a simplex the cap root is affine in the vertex coordinate. The two
quantile bands realize the bathtub bound and Jensen simultaneously.
The equality constraint puts the cap plane through the full density
centroid, not an independently chosen projected surrogate. Boundary
bands are null sets for the relevant absolutely continuous measure.
Consequently the scalar minimum is an attained sharp constant for the
stated density class.

The explicit lower bounds follow by dropping the separate-cap mass
constraint in the bathtub optimization and then using r>=s+alpha-1.
At alpha=0 and alpha=1 they recover gamma_d as claimed. Their use for
arbitrary optimized mixed capacities would require an additional measure
representation which has not been proved and is not asserted here.

## 3. Additional marginal example check

I read the new n=3,d=3 construction in
`candidate dc03bcfaffa32184` and ran its updated
exact verifier successfully. The strictly convex polynomial objective
attains its minimum on the rational rectangle. Its four whole-side
gradient signs exclude the boundary, so its exact critical equations
give the required integer moments. The affine-root identity gives the
full mixed centroid in the central fiber. The displayed vertical cap
has its boundary fiber included, and the rational upper bound 367/1000
is strictly below 1/e by the certified factorial-series estimate.
This cap is not claimed to violate the OC constant.
